chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Mas'ud al-Mila'i, from Habba al-'Urni. He said:

Abdullah ibn Umar saw two men disputing over the head of Ammar (may God be pleased with him). One said: 'I killed him!' and the other said: 'I killed him!' So Ibn Umar said: 'They are disputing over which of them will enter the Fire first!' Then he said: 'I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: His killer and his plunderer are in the Fire.' When this reached Mu'awiya, he said: 'We did not kill him; rather, the one who brought him killed him.'

Shaykh Abu Ja'far ibn Babuwayh (may God be pleased with him) [responded]: By this logic, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would be the killer of Hamza (may God be pleased with him) and the killer of the martyrs with him, because he (peace be upon him and his family) is the one who brought them.

key_terms.النار: The Fire (Hellfire), the punishment awaiting those who killed Ammar
key_terms.سالبه: His plunderer/despoiler, referring to the one who stripped Ammar's body
key_terms.عمار: Ammar ibn Yasir, a prominent companion of the Prophet whose killing at Siffin was prophesied

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the killer of Ammar ibn Yasir?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the aftermath of the killing of Ammar ibn Yasir at the Battle of Siffin (37 AH), where two soldiers from Mu'awiya's army fought over who killed him. Abdullah ibn Umar reminded them of the Prophet's warning that Ammar's killer and plunderer would be in Hellfire. When Mu'awiya tried to deflect blame by claiming 'the one who brought him to battle killed him,' al-Saduq refuted this specious argument by noting that the same logic would make the Prophet responsible for the death of Hamza and other martyrs at Uhud.
